# @al-rayhaanat/tokens

Zero dependencies. Every other package depends on this one.

`packages/tokens/brand.json` (DTCG) is the only place a raw value is written. Everything
in `dist/` is generated by `tokens/style-dictionary.config.mjs`:

| Output | Consumer |
| --- | --- |
| `dist/tokens.css` | every web app — import once, at the root |
| `dist/tokens.ts` | React logic, chart series, motion helpers |
| `dist/tailwind.preset.cjs` | Next.js apps (`presets: [require('@al-rayhaanat/tokens/tailwind')]`) |
| `dist/_tokens.scss` | legacy / non-React modules |
| `dist/figma.variables.json` | designers |
| `../slides/dist/pptx.theme.js` | generated decks |
| `fonts/KanzalLulu-Regular.ttf` | self-hosted Arabic face |

```bash
npm run build:tokens     # style-dictionary build
```

## How to consume

```css
/* app/globals.css */
@import "@al-rayhaanat/tokens/tokens.css";
```

```jsx
<html lang="en" dir="ltr" data-theme="light">   {/* or lang="ar" dir="rtl", data-theme="dark" */}
```

Products reference **semantic** names only — `var(--surface)`, `var(--text-muted)`,
`var(--interactive)`. The ramps (`--color-crimson-500`) exist so semantics can be
composed; application code must not reach for them. Lint fails the build on a raw
hex, an arbitrary Tailwind value, or a physical margin/padding property.

## Colour

Everything comes out of the mark. Crimson is the core, rose the inner petal rank,
and **sand** — the warm neutral ramp carrying every ground and surface — is grown
from the outer petal, `#f5ecdf`, which is the canvas itself. A second cool
**slate** ramp exists for dense data, where warm greys muddy figures.

| Ramp | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `sand` 50–950 | Warm neutral: canvas, surfaces, rules, warm ink |
| `slate` 50–950 | Cool neutral: text and chrome in tables and ledgers |
| `crimson` 50–950 | Primary — the single interactive voice |
| `rose` 50–950 | Secondary — tints, tags, brand moments |
| `green` / `amber` / `blue` / `clay` | Success / warning / info / danger |
| `motif` | The mark's three layers, opaque, on the mark only |

### Palettes

Six combinations, exported as `--palette-<name>-{ground,surface,ink,accent,support}`
and as `palettes` in `tokens.ts`. One palette per surface — never two on a page.

| Palette | For |
| --- | --- |
| **Bindery** (light, default) | Admin portal, member app, forms |
| **Ledger** (light, data) | Dense tables, reconciliation — cool neutrals |
| **Petal** (light, brand) | Covers, landing, empty states |
| **Colophon** (dark) | Deck dividers, dark chrome |
| **Proof** (print) | Reports, statements, anything photocopied |
| **Signal** (status) | Feedback layered onto any palette above |

Crimson 600 is the solid fill (white on it clears 4.5:1); crimson 500 is the mark
and the focus ring. Danger is **clay**, a warmer red, so destruction never reads
as ordinary brand emphasis — and never hue alone: always an icon or a label too.

## Type — two scripts, one scale

Cormorant Garamond sets display (above 21px only; it goes frail below), Lora sets
body and interface text, IBM Plex Mono sets code and identifiers. Weights stop at
600.

Arabic is **Kanz al-Lulu Regular**, self-hosted from `fonts/`, scoped by
`unicode-range` so mixed-direction text picks the right face per character with no
wrapper component.

### What the font file actually says

Read directly from the TTF, so neither blocking question is open any more:

- **Unicode-compliant, not legacy.** 127 codepoints in U+0600–06FF, 277 in
  Presentation-A (the double-key ligature forms), 88 in Presentation-B, all eight
  harakat plus shadda and superscript alef, Eastern digits — and **zero** Private
  Use Area mappings. GSUB carries `aalt ccmp init medi fina isol liga rlig`; GPOS
  is present, so mark positioning is real. Store Unicode, render with the font;
  **no encoding boundary is needed.**
- **`fsType = 0`** — the font's own bits permit installable embedding without
  restriction. Get the distributor's web licence in writing anyway.
- **Vertical metrics:** unitsPerEm 2048, win ascent 2220, descent 1200 →
  **line-height 1.67 minimum** or marks clip. So Arabic leading is
  `max(latin × 1.22, 1.70)`, not a flat multiplier: at display steps the
  multiplier alone gave 1.42 and clipped. Every step ships as
  `--text-ar-*` / `--leading-ar-*`, and `--leading-ar-floor` is the floor.

Still to do in CI: subset and convert to `.woff2` (~500 KB → ~90 KB) and preload
it — a flash of fallback Arabic is far more disruptive than the Latin equivalent.
The name table in this build is empty, so the `@font-face` family name in
`tokens.css` is what defines it.

## Contrast audit

Measured from the tokens, not asserted (WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text
and UI bounds). All pairs pass in both modes.

| Pair | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| text-primary on canvas | 14.79 | 16.56 |
| text-primary on surface | 17.02 | 14.98 |
| text-secondary on surface | 8.61 | 11.27 |
| text-muted on surface | 5.09 | 7.05 |
| interactive on surface / canvas | 7.59 / 6.59 | 8.16 / 9.03 |
| white on interactive-solid | 5.75 | 5.75 |
| border-control on surface | 5.09 | 4.99 |
| focus-ring on canvas | 3.78 | 6.26 |
| success / warning / danger / info on surface | 6.53 / 5.83 / 5.99 / 7.89 | 9.10 / 9.84 / 8.51 / 7.87 |

`--border` (decorative separators, 1.46) is deliberately below 3:1; control and
input boundaries use `--border-control`.

## Assumptions on record

- **Numerals**: Eastern Arabic-Indic (٠١٢٣) in Arabic UI prose and headings;
  Western (0123) for IDs, phone numbers and anything copied into another system.
  `tnum` on every figure standing in a column.
- **Narrow-screen tables**: horizontal scroll with a sticky first column, applied
  everywhere. No card fallback — it breaks column comparison, which is the point.
- **Modes**: light and dark, both first-class.
- **Lisan al-Dawat content** in the foundation boards is placeholder MSA
  vocabulary. The clipping tests are only meaningful against real supplied strings.
